Authentic XXXX is never light, fluffy, perfumed, fibrous, or finely milled. There are no regional variations within XXXX that produce a pale or perfumed version. Anything that is light in XXXX, strawlike, or scented is not authentic XXXX and is typically a blend of unrelated herbs or fillers.

narrative:
Formal complaint regarding Chase checking account for Regulation E violation, wrongful denial of fraud claim, and agent misconduct.

FACTS : During a recent relocation I lost my Chase debit card. It was recovered the next day. During that window, 19 unauthorized transactions totaling {$7200.00} posted to my account. I did not make, authorize, or furnish my card to anyone including any family member for any of these transactions. I reported the loss and unauthorized charges to Chase promptly upon discovery on XX/XX/year>. My account now carries a negative balance of approximately - {$350.00}, exposing me to additional overdraft fees on funds that never should have left my account.

CHASE WRONGFULLY DENIED THE CLAIM in apparent violation of : - Electronic Fund Transfer Act, 15 U.S.C. 1693 - Regulation E, 12 C.F.R. Part 1005 Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.2 ( m ), an " unauthorized electronic fund transfer '' includes a transfer by a person other than the consumer without actual authority and from which the consumer receives no benefit. Transactions made with a lost or stolen card by someone the consumer did not furnish the card to fall squarely within this definition.

Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.6, my liability is strictly limited by federal statute not by Chase 's internal policy.

Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11, Chase was required to : ( a ) conduct a good-faith investigation, ( b ) complete it within 10 business days OR extend to 45 days only with provisional credit, ( c ) provide a written explanation of any denial, and ( d ) provide the documents relied upon upon request. I have received none of these in a form meeting federal requirements.

AGENT MISCONDUCT : 1. On a recorded call, the agent handling my claim was laughing and joking while discussing {$7200.00} in unauthorized transactions. Treating a fraud claim of this size as entertainment is unacceptable and demonstrates bad-faith handling.

2. When I requested a supervisor, the agent instructed me to call back in exactly 14 minutes. I called back at the exact time instructed. The operator stated the department was closed and to call back the next day. This was either a deliberate misdirection to block escalation before close of business, or a false statement by the agent. Either way it is evidence of bad-faith claim handling.

I am formally requesting Chase pull and review all call recordings tied to my claim. I have documented dates, times, and substance of every call.

LITIGATION HOLD : Chase is on formal notice to preserve : all call recordings, agent notes, internal case messages, case file documents, transaction logs, device authentication records, IP/location data, and authorization records tied to the 19 disputed transactions. DESIRED RESOLUTION : 1. Full reimbursement of {$7200.00} in unauthorized
transactions 2. Reversal of all related overdraft fees and restoration of account to positive balance 3. Written Regulation E-compliant explanation per 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 4. Review of agent conduct on my claim 5. Written response within 15 days as required If not resolved, I will pursue : OCC complaint, Virginia Attorney General Consumer Protection complaint, and civil action under 15 U.S.C. 1693m for actual damages, statutory damages, costs, and attorney 's fees.

I am filing this complaint against Citibank / Citi Cards for failing to properly investigate and resolve a billing dispute filed under the Fair Credit Billing Act.

Summary of the dispute : On XX/XX/year>, I was charged {$940.00} by XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX ( XXXX, PA ) for a plumbing service call at my rental property ( XXXX, PA XXXX ). The work performed was described as clearing a blocked sewer main line using a cable snaking machine. I am disputing {$800.00} of this charge on the grounds that the service was not completed as expected.

Key evidence of failed service : Only seven ( 7 ) days after the first visit, on XX/XX/year>, the same plumbing company ( XXXX XXXX ) was called back to the same property for the identical sewer blockage problem and charged me an additional {$420.00} ( Invoice # XXXX ). The second technicians own invoice notes confirm that the fresh air inlet the exact access point used on the first visit was still covered, and that the house trap was narrow filled with dirt and mulch. The technician recommended a hydrojet and camera inspection, which should have been performed during the first visit given the severity of the blockage. In other words, XXXX XXXX own documentation proves the first visit failed to resolve the problem. 

Citis handling of the dispute : I filed a dispute with Citi on XX/XX/year> ( Citi Case ID : XXXX ) on the grounds of goods/services not as expected. Citi issued a conditional credit of {$800.00} at that time. I subsequently sent Citi a detailed written dispute letter via certified mail, including both invoices and photographic evidence showing the severity of the initial blockage and the condition of the drain at the second visit. Despite this documentation including the merchants own second invoice as evidence of an incomplete first repair Citi sided with the merchant and reversed the conditional credit, holding me responsible for the full disputed amount. 

Why I believe Citis decision was incorrect : Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, a billing dispute based on services not rendered as expected requires the card issuer to conduct a reasonable investigation. I provided Citi with two invoices from the same merchant one for the disputed charge and a second one, dated just seven days later, for the same work at the same location. The second invoice is not a separate, unrelated service : it is direct, contemporaneous evidence from the merchant itself that the first repair was incomplete. A reasonable investigation would have recognized this. Instead, Citi appears to have accepted the merchants response without adequately weighing this evidence.
